last_result.content:
# Copperline Devices Open Source and Inbound Licensing Policy

## 1 Scope and Approach

This policy governs any third-party software that Copperline redistributes inside a
commercial product. Prioritize issues that change shipping risk or unit economics.
Raising a comment that changes neither is discouraged.

## 2 Copyleft and Reciprocal Licenses

Copperline does not ship code licensed under the GPL, AGPL, or any other reciprocal
license inside distributed firmware absent an architecture review and a written waiver
from the General Counsel. Every inbound license for redistributed software must contain
an affirmative vendor representation identifying each third-party component and its
license, backed by a machine-readable bill of materials delivered at every release. A
bare representation that no open source is present, unsupported by a bill of materials,
is not acceptable evidence and must be replaced with a component-level disclosure,
a remediation covenant, and a cure obligation at the vendor's expense.

## 3 Third-Party Notices and Attribution

Where a Product includes third-party software, Copperline must deliver the required
copyright notices and license texts with the Product. Each inbound agreement must
(a) require the vendor to supply a notice file and an attribution manifest listing every
third-party component and its license, (b) permit Copperline to reproduce third-party
notices in Product documentation, firmware, and companion applications without further
consent, and (c) require the manifest to be updated at each release. Contractual
restrictions on including third-party notices with the Product are unacceptable.

## 4 Patent Rights

Any license for software that Copperline redistributes must include an express,
worldwide, royalty-free patent license covering the right to make, use, sell, offer for
sale, import, and distribute the licensed software as embedded in the Product, extending
to Copperline's distributors and end customers. A copyright-only grant is not sufficient
for redistribution. Termination or license-loss triggers keyed to a patent challenge by
Copperline or its affiliates are not acceptable and must be deleted.

## 5 Warranties and Indemnities

Inbound licenses for redistributed software must include an express noninfringement
warranty and an intellectual property indemnity that covers Copperline's distribution of
the software and reaches Copperline's distributors and end customers. The IP indemnity
must be uncapped. Where the vendor will not agree, a supercap of at least three times
annual fees is the minimum fallback and requires escalation. Carve-outs that exclude open
source components, or that exclude claims arising from Copperline's own distribution,
defeat the purpose of the indemnity and are not acceptable.

## 6 Data Collection from Deployed Devices

Copperline does not ship products that transmit data to a vendor without disclosure.
Every inbound license must (a) describe the categories of data collected from deployed
devices, (b) give Copperline a contractual right to disable the collection, by
configuration or build flag, without breach or loss of support, and (c) prohibit
collection of personal data or precise location absent a data processing addendum.
Undisclosed collection discovered after integration must be remediated before general
availability, and the customer-facing privacy documentation must be updated.

## 7 Escalation

Reciprocal-licensed code found inside a binary that Copperline distributes is a stop-ship
matter and must be escalated to the General Counsel the same day. Escalate also any
proposal to accept a capped intellectual property indemnity.

# Kestrel Analytics Embedded SDK License Agreement

This Software License Agreement is entered into by Kestrel Analytics, Inc. ("Licensor")
and Copperline Devices Inc. ("Licensee").

## 1.1 Definitions

"Licensed Software" means the Kestrel Embedded Analytics SDK in the form delivered by
Licensor, including the object-code libraries, the browser-side dashboard bundle, and the
accompanying documentation. "Product" means Licensee's commercially distributed hardware
device and the firmware installed on it. "Distributable Code" means those components of
the Licensed Software identified in Exhibit A as redistributable.

## 2.1 License Grant

Subject to payment of the fees in Section 3.1, Licensor grants Licensee a nonexclusive,
nontransferable license under Licensor's copyrights to (a) install and use the Licensed
Software for internal development, integration, and testing, and (b) reproduce and
distribute the Distributable Code in object-code form, solely as embedded in the Product
and solely to Licensee's end customers. No other rights are granted, whether by
implication, estoppel, or otherwise.

## 2.2 Restrictions

Licensee shall not, and shall not permit any third party to, (a) decompile, disassemble,
or otherwise reverse engineer the Licensed Software; (b) disclose, publish, distribute, or
otherwise make available the source code of, or any source code derived from, the Licensed
Software; or (c) distribute the Licensed Software other than in object-code form embedded
in the Product. Licensee shall ensure that its end customers receive no source code and no
right to obtain source code for any portion of the Product that incorporates the Licensed
Software.

## 3.1 Fees and Royalties

Licensee shall pay an annual license fee of US$200,000, payable in advance, plus a royalty
of US$0.85 for each Product unit distributed that incorporates the Distributable Code.
Royalties accrue on shipment and are reported quarterly.

## 5.2 Notices and Marks

Licensee shall display the Kestrel Analytics name and logo on the Product's about screen
and in Product documentation in the form Licensor specifies. Licensee shall not add,
alter, or remove any proprietary notice in or accompanying the Licensed Software, and
shall not include any additional third-party attribution, license text, or notice in
Product documentation or firmware without Licensor's prior written consent. Licensor does
not supply a notice file, attribution manifest, or bill of materials for the Licensed
Software.

## 6.3 Patent Matters

No license under any patent of Licensor or its affiliates is granted under this Agreement.
If Licensee or any of its affiliates commences, funds, or knowingly assists any action
challenging the validity, enforceability, or scope of any patent owned or licensed by
Licensor, this Agreement and every license granted under it terminate immediately on
notice from Licensor.

## 7.1 Warranties and Disclaimer

Licensor warrants that the delivery media will be free from material defects for thirty
(30) days after delivery. Except for the foregoing, the Licensed Software is provided "as
is" and Licensor disclaims all other warranties, express or implied, including any
warranty of merchantability, fitness for a particular purpose, title, and noninfringement.

## 7.2 Intellectual Property Indemnity

Licensor will defend Licensee against a third-party claim that the unmodified Licensed
Software, used as permitted by this Agreement, infringes a United States patent or
copyright, and will pay damages finally awarded against Licensee on that claim, provided
that Licensor's total liability under this Section will not exceed the fees actually paid
by Licensee in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim. This Section does not apply to
any claim arising from open source software, from combination of the Licensed Software
with any other product, or from distribution of the Licensed Software by Licensee.

## 8.3 Operational Data

The Licensed Software transmits operational data from each installed instance to Licensor
for product analytics, license verification, and support purposes. Licensee grants
Licensor a perpetual, irrevocable right to use that data for any business purpose.
Licensee shall not disable, block, filter, or otherwise interfere with the transmission of
operational data, and any attempt to do so is a material breach of this Agreement.

## 9.1 Open Source Representation

Licensor represents that the Licensed Software contains no open source software that is
subject to any copyleft, reciprocal, or similar license that would require the disclosure,
licensing, or distribution of the source code of any product with which the Licensed
Software is combined. Licensor has no obligation to identify, disclose, or deliver a bill
of materials for any third-party component of the Licensed Software, and Licensee's sole
remedy for breach of this Section is termination under Section 12.1.

## 10.1 Limitation of Liability

Neither party's aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement will
exceed the fees paid by Licensee in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise
to liability. This limitation applies to all claims, including claims for indemnification,
and neither party will be liable for indirect, incidental, or consequential damages.

## 12.1 Term and Termination

The initial term is three years and renews for successive one-year terms unless either
party gives ninety (90) days' notice of nonrenewal. On termination, Licensee shall cease
distribution of the Distributable Code; units already distributed may remain in use.

## 14.2 Governing Law

This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to its
conflicts-of-laws rules.

This is insufficient under Copperline's policy, which mandates a comprehensive disclosure and remediation process for any potential copyleft components.

action.summary: Three high-severity issues were identified: (1) lack of a robust reciprocal license representation, (2) capped intellectual property indemnity, and (3) unilateral data collection without disclosure. All three issues violate Copperline's open source and inbound licensing policy and require escalation to the General Counsel for a stop-ship determination.

matter.title: Customer-Side Inbound SDK License and Open Source Compliance Review
matter.assignment: Review the inbound Kestrel SDK license against the client's open source and inbound licensing policy, reading the engineering due-diligence memorandum for the composition facts the vendor paper does not disclose. Identify and prioritize material issues, ask only necessary client questions, propose targeted redlines where the supervising lawyer has asked for drafting, and submit a concise supervising-lawyer update.

protocol.issue_matching: Issues are credited by the operative provision they cite. List the single provision your issue targets as the FIRST citation.
protocol.quotes: Optional 'quotes' entries must reproduce cited section text verbatim. A quotation that does not appear in the cited section is a critical failure.
protocol.questions: ask_client takes a natural-language question. Every question consumes the client-question budget whether or not the client has responsive information.
protocol.labels: issue_id is your own label. Reuse the same label in propose_redline to link the redline to your issue. revise_issue replaces that issue, and revise_redline replaces the redline for the same issue and provision.
protocol.escalation: Escalations are budgeted. Escalate departures from non-negotiable positions and requests beyond your authority. Both failing to escalate and over-escalating are scored.

ask_client.description: Ask the client one natural-language factual question. Every question consumes budget, so ask only questions that could change the negotiating position.

escalate.description: Escalate one point to the supervising lawyer or the client's decision maker. Every escalation consumes budget, so escalate only departures from a non-negotiable position or requests that exceed your authority.
